newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse shows short-term debentures index.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse shows short-term debentures index.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) presented its index of short-term debentures on Friday for bourse trading.
"We have established an index of short-term debentures as an indicator showing tendencies and quality of transactions on the BSE," Pava Zecevic, exchange director, said.
"Unlike an index reflecting movements in shares, the BSE index mirrors conditions under which companies and banks borrow and repay their debt," she told a news conference.
The BSE index was calculated with the most heavily bourse-traded financial instruments based on volume, interest rates and maturity.

"As the trade in shares has not developed yet, we had to calculate the index on short-term commercial papers and treasury bills, the segment which dominated trade on the BSE since it was founded in 1989," said the BSE's Milko Stimac.
"Trade in those papers gives the real overall picture of the situation on the financial market," he said.
The BSE took 1996 as the index base.

Stimac said the index, which the BSE calls the Belgrade bourse index of short-term debentures, will be published in the BSE weekly reports because the daily volume was too low for daily reports. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 311 4254
